messages.subject: how to "flush" dynamic UI components?
parts:
My app use handsontable (preferred to datatable for its write-in-cell capabilities). To drive changes to the table I use also dynamic sliders to spread selected values over months.

This is a simplified workflow:
1. User selects (with another UI component) which categorical elements to spread. 
2. The slider appears set to zero, min & max.  
3. The user selects a value on the slider, say +100, to spread
4. The table is updated dynamically
5. Repeat for different values
...
n. The table is saved with an action button, and
n+1. The UI reverts to the original status, e.g. with no dynamic UI component displayed.
n+2. The user may continue with another iteration & new changes

The problem I have is that the value at input$<programmed slider name> does not "disappear", even if the UI is not displayed.  If I go back and try to read that input variable it still does exist.

To bypass the problem every time I save the table I change the name of the variable (i.e. adding to it a progressive number with paste0).
I am conscious though that I have all these "old" variable names with their "old" status probably in some shiny cache.

I recognise that in some circumstances the persistence of these values is a feature.  On the other hand if there is a simple method to FLUSH all these "old" elements it would be great.

As a side note, I know I could at least re-position all the sliders in their initial status resetting values to zero, but this adds unwanted complexity (e.g. to find which sliders were used *during the entire user session* by the user?) to an already very complex piece of code. If I could flush them easily as they never existed before it would be much simpler for my code.

Is there a way to do this that I've missed??
